utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Registrar. Could we have the appearances for the day, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Dan Saxon, Bronagh McKenna, and Carmela Javier for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Saxon. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone participating in the proceedings. Novak Lukic and Boris Zorko are representing Mr. Perisic today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Good morning, Mr. Skrbic. Just to remind you again - I know you know it already - that you're still bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of the testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Thank you so much. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Good morning, General Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please show the witness P2719, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Skrbic, I'm going to show you very briefly one more document that is related to the subject of training; however, I'm not going to ask you any substantive questions about training. I need to show you this document to see if you can clarify an acronym.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we could make both versions a bit bigger, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Skrbic, you'll see this is a document dated the 15th of April, 1995. It's from Commander Ratko Mladic from the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, and it's addressed to the Yugoslav Army General Staff, personally to the chief. If you look at the full paragraph in this document you'll see -- in English at least it says: "Please approve that it be approved that two officers - instructors from the Pancevo ..." And then there is an acronym "OBS," with the diacritic, "C."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: OBO -- actually, I'm a bit lost. You talked of the 15th of April. The document I have is dated the 20th of April and --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour, because the page I have in front of me seems not to be in the same order. Can we go to the next document, please -- the next page in both languages. Well, it's not exactly the document I was looking for, but it is part of this exhibit and we see the same acronym.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Skrbic, can you tell us what the Pancevo BOSC stood for, what that acronym means or meant?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Saxon, this acronym, BOSC, means security and intelligence training centre of Pancevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And that was a VJ --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Oops.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard the interpreters repeating the same interpretation that is in the document, but I think that the training centre is not a correct term. It should literally be translated as schooling centre because schooling is normally related to education not training. Therefore, I would ask the interpreters to correct that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: As the interpreters did, interpreter's note.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure I understand what the interpreter means by "as the interpreters did, interpreter's note." I don't know whether they mean they agree that it is "schooling" and not "training," and if they don't mean that, then I want to say to Mr. Lukic do you want to swap places with the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The literal translation would be schooling centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can we go to the next page in both languages, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if you can -- this is the document that I was referring to initially, General Skrbic. It's part of the same exhibit, 2719.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we could enlarge, please, the middle of the B/C/S version, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And so, General, this is the original request dated 15th April 1995. It's from Ratko Mladic from the Main Staff of the VRS to the Yugoslav Army General Staff, personally to the chief. So this request, actually now that you've -- we've clarified the acronym and clarified the English, this is a request that two VJ officers who normally work at a VJ schooling centre extend their engagement at the Banja Luka military school centre of the VRS. Is that a fair interpretation?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We can leave this document now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Skrbic, you are aware, are you not, that in 1995 this Tribunal indicted Ratko Mladic for his responsibility for events at Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. What were you actually asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm simply asking you to confirm that you have knowledge that this Tribunal has indicted Ratko Mladic for his responsibility -- excuse me, his alleged responsibility for the events that occurred in Srebrenica in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the year, but I know that the indictment has been issued, as you said, in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Can you recall when you became aware that General Mladic was indicted by this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you recall approximately when you became aware that Ratko Mladic had been indicted by this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember even approximately. I only remember the event itself. A son of my colleague told me that there was an indictment on the internet, I looked at it, but I don't remember which date it was when I did that. Later on I reviewed the indictment on several occasions on the internet, and I think you know that all the indictments are available on the internet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please show the witness Exhibit D346.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We're going to show you, General Skrbic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you need private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. Yes, I do. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Skrbic, this is an excerpt from one of the notebooks of General Mladic that my colleague Novak Lukic showed you last week.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we just move the cursor down just a bit in the B/C/S version. Just a bit, bit more. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This was the excerpt of the meeting on the 10th of December, 1995, between members of the VRS Main Staff, including yourself, General Mladic, and President Lilic of the FRY, General Perisic, and some other members of the VJ General Staff. And I just want to focus for a moment on the notes taken by General Mladic of what President Lilic is saying there on the first page. We see, according to General Mladic's notes: "Greeted and thanked us for everything. "We have done so far for our people. "The French are convinced that the pilots are here ... "Today is the last day for us to tell France what we know about the pilots. "We will sign, Momo and I, that nobody will be extradited to The Hague Tribunal." And it's that last notation that I'd like to ask you about. Help us with this, please, General. The point President Lilic was making and that General Mladic was noting down was that as part of the FRY government's negotiations with the French government for the return of the French pilots, Zoran Lilic and General Perisic would make a written promise that the FRY would not extradite General Mladic to this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, I can confirm what you said about this book. Your Honours, I had an opportunity to look at one of the books and I became convinced of what I wanted to become convinced. One thing should be crossed out here because General Skrbic is mentioned here twice and there was only one General Skrbic present there --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Skrbic let me stop you, please, with all due respect. Actually, my colleague Mr. Lukic already explained that last week, that it's simply a mistake, that your name was written there twice. That's very clear to everyone, so you need not worry about that.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm not focused enough and I'm not able to read the transcript in English, therefore I'm sorry. So President Lilic, when he came to this meeting, he was indeed the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. However, he came there more for the purpose of putting forward his authority in terms of discussing the fate of the pilots. We on the Main Staff had no knowledge about their whereabouts or whether they were alive or not --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Skrbic --

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- it seems that he knew --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm very --

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- let me tell you just this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Okay.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I wanted just to respond to what you said. It wasn't us who offered any views about the Hague Tribunal, but I think that that was an unrealistic promise made to Ratko Mladic because no one from the outside could decide what the Tribunal and the Prosecution would do about anyone. So that was just a political statement which seemed to be the most important one at the moment, and the crucial thing had to do with the French pilot.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Whether it was an unrealistic promise or not, the bottom line is that was the promise that was made; right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the promise was made, but it was an unrealistic one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. To date, General Skrbic, Ratko Mladic remains at large; isn't that right? He's still a fugitive?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know in which direction Mr. Saxon is trying to go. I don't think that this particular question is relevant, so I would appreciate if he would tell us what his intentions with this line of questioning are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness has given an interpretation that has told us a particular promise was made. He's then given us his interpretation or belief that the promise made at the time was unrealistic. And I'm simply trying to confirm -- well, discuss with him or explore with the witness the fact that this -- to date General Mladic still has not been extradited to this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, for the Chamber the main problem is of what relevance is all of that to the guilt or innocence of Mr. Perisic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, it's relevant to allegations in the indictment, for example, that Mr. Perisic assisted in the harbouring of General Perisic -- of General Mladic after the time that he became a fugitive, after the time that he was indicted by this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you going to attribute this kind of -- this notes here to Mr. Perisic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I don't understand your question, Your Honour. I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're saying Mr. Perisic is alleged to have assisted Mladic not to be extradited to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And I'm saying: Are you then attributing what Lilic is saying to Mr. Perisic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The short answer is yes, Your Honour, because what Lilic says is: We will sign, Momo and I, Momcilo -- Momo was the nickname of our accused, that nobody will be extradited to The Hague Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand that, but I don't understand why Mr. Saxon asked the previous question, that is to say why -- whether the witness is aware that Mr. Mladic is still at large. I don't see the link between the two questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's simply a follow-up question to the witness's comment that this promise that was made at this meeting was unrealistic. The Prosecution's point, Your Honour, if I may put it to the witness, is to this day -- it's -- the witness's position is that this was an unrealistic promise. The Prosecution's position is it apparently is -- was realistic because to this day General Mladic has not been extradited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The question is allowed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The fact, General Skrbic, that Ratko Mladic to this day has not been extradited to The Hague is an indication that at least to some degree the promise made was somewhat realistic, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't agree with you. Your Honours, allow me to go back to the statement of Mr. Lilic, the president of the FRY. He didn't make any promises to General Perisic. The document that was signed, which I hadn't seen, but this document as we were later on told by the commander of the Main Staff of the VRS was signed solely by Mr. Lilic, the president of the FRY. I think that this document could be found here at the Tribunal maybe in some other case, so probably someone should seek and look for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before I allow Mr. Lukic to speak, you said, Mr. Skrbic, that President Lilic didn't make any promises to General Perisic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: General Perisic did not make any promises.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, he didn't make any promises to General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Right. Now interpreter's correction, is that correction also incorrect? I would imagine so. Now -- okay, he didn't make any promises to General Mladic. Then the next sentence says "the document that was" -- just give me a chance, please. You said: "The document that was signed, which I hadn't seen, but this document as we were later on told by the commander of the Main Staff of the VRS was signed solely by Mr. Lilic, president of the FRY." What document are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm talking about the promises contained in this document. Your Honours, I'm sorry for being repetitive. General Perisic did not make any promises with regard to Ratko Mladic. It was only President Lilic who did that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand that, Mr. Skrbic. Don't confuse us, please. I'm trying to understand your answer so that we know exactly what you are saying. We understand that General Perisic from this document that is on the screen here has said nothing in the meeting and that what is being written here by General Mladic in his diary has -- doesn't say General Perisic said anything. But it says that General -- President Lilic and General Momo are going to sign something that nobody will be extradited. Now, your answer, you say: "The document that was signed, which" you "hadn't seen ... was signed solely by President Lilic." My simple question to you is what document is that you are referring to that was signed by President Lilic, the one that you say it can be found in some other case in this Tribunal. That's all I want to know, which document is this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the document, as the commander told us, contains about seven to nine bullet points. All of those are promises about schools being reconstructed, compensations made for the French pilots, and not only that, a number of other bullet points including this particular one regarding the Hague Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Now the problem is now that you are talking about a document which we don't have before us that you know about that nobody else seems to know anything about in this court. Now, if you could stay with the document that is before us, it would be helpful, unless you are able to give us this document -- this other document that you are talking about. But if you are not able to give it to us, it's not going to be helpful talking about it because we don't have it. Thank you so much. Mr. Lukic, you were on your feet.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, could you please switch off your mike. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I wanted to point to some discrepancies. I believe that the interpreters on page 10 and line 19, the interpreters have corrected their mistakes from the previous paragraph that Mr. Skrbic also confirmed for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, but then that's no reason for you to stand up. If they've made the correction, then you just stay put.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I was on my feet at the -- the interpreters had still not corrected their mistakes. That's when I got up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. I'm sorry. Okay, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. While we're still in private session, can we please show the witness Exhibit D344?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Skrbic, I'm going to show you in a moment another excerpt from one of General Mladic's notebooks. This is the excerpt from the meeting on the 12th of August, 1994, about the Contact Group plan. And you'll recall that Mr. Lukic and you had some discussion about this meeting and that plan last Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, this discussion begins at page 11742 of the transcript. And I'm wondering if we could please move to page 5 in the English version, please, and the corresponding page in B/C/S I'm -- I don't have in front of me, but it's probably page 3 or 4. And now I'm seeing --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is page 5. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please -- one moment, please. Can we please move back one page in English, please. I apologise to Your Honours. Can we please move back one more page in English, and if we can please find -- you'll see near the top of the page, and General Perisic is -- according to Ratko Mladic's notes, this is General Perisic speaking. It starts on the very first page of this excerpt. Can we please find the corresponding page in Serbo-Croat where we see $3.5 billion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you see, General Skrbic, in your version --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In B/C/S it's page 3, the upper part of the page, that's where a reference is made to the figures that Mr. Saxon is now referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm very grateful to Mr. Lukic for his help.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Skrbic, if you take a look towards the top of the page, it says -- General Perisic is speaking here and -- according to the notes, and it says: "The FRY is isolated. The Serbian and Montenegrin people do not have the resources to help you." And then it says: "Of the $3.5 billion received, we have set aside $750 million for the army." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: By the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really apologise to Mr. Saxon. I can see a major discrepancy between the original and the translation of this document. I already overlooked one mistake. Could Mr. Skrbic ask the B/C/S version, the second sentence or the second line, could you please blow that up for him and if he reads it in our own language and if it is translated, you will see that there is a major discrepancy.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can I answer, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm reading the second sentence. "From the $3.5 billion requested for the army, $750 million would be allocated for the army."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That doesn't make sense to me. You can't say you've requested 3.5 billion for the army and then you've set aside 750 for the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Skrbic, would it be a fair interpretation of this notation that of the $3.5 billion requested for the total budget --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But the interpretation said "for the army."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I understand that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I understand that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Would it be a fair interpretation that of the $3.5 billion requested for the total budget, $750 million would be allocated for the army; is that a fair interpretation?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that was another promise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I understand that. My question for you is the following: The phrase "for the army," General Perisic by the phrase "the army," was including the VJ, the VRS, and the SVK; right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He means the Army of Yugoslavia, and only that part that concerns the salaries of the members of the 30th and 40th staff centre is part of this plan. And with regard to this figure, it would be a minute amount, an unsignificant -- insignificant amount.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, at that time, summer of 1994, were you privy to the requested budget of the Army of Yugoslavia? Did you have access to that?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So you are just surmising then what part of the requested budget for the VJ would be going to support the persons of -- in the 30th and 40th staff centre; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: During the same discussion that you had with Mr. Lukic last week about this meeting - and this is at 11748 of the transcript - you testified when discussing the position of the FRY presented at that meeting by General Perisic, Mr. Lukic read to you some of the notes which said, for example: "If the plan was not accepted, then a series of measures would be implemented. Some had already been implemented." And Mr. Lukic asked you to explain what that meant and at lines 11 to 13 you replied: "What is meant by this is that the border was closed in every sense, the border between the FRY and the Republika Srpska at the Drina River and other places." Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I just want to make sure that I understand your position, General. Your position is that by the time this meeting on the 12th of August, 1994, took place, nothing would move across the border of the FRY and the Republika Srpska, with the exception of humanitarian assistance. Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is my position because the barrier was not complete, not for all the goods.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, we can go back into public session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the chamber please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please show the witness what is Exhibit P628, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, if you take a look, please, at this document, the date at the top is very -- the actual year at the top is a bit difficult to read. It says 15 August 19 and the last two numbers are difficult to read, but at the bottom we see a date stamp of the special units of the VJ from 17 August 1994. And you'll see this document, it's from the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia, sector for logistics. And you'll see at the bottom it's signed by General Perisic, Chief of the General Staff. And in this document General Perisic is referring to an order of the president of the FRY, dated the 18th of February, 1994, pursuant to which General Perisic issued an instruction for replenishment of the 30th and 40th Personnel Centre with material supplies, which was submitted to you under -- and then he gives the number of that order of February. And then General Perisic goes on to say the following: "Despite constant warnings, certain commanding officers of the VJ disobeyed the order and issued equipment for the needs of the 30th and 40th Personnel Centre without authorisation." He refers to disciplinary and criminal procedures that are under way. And then he gives a series of four instructions, and number 1 is: "Warn all those issuing orders and all material organs to strictly implement the measures and procedures from the mentioned instruction. "2. Prevent the unauthorised issuance of weaponry and military equipment." Have you been able to read along with me?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have been able to read along with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, there's nothing in this order of General Perisic that says, "Stop providing equipment and materiel to the VRS, is there?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And so basically in summary form General Perisic is saying if you're going to give materiel and equipment to the VRS, do it the way I told you to do it; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that's your interpretation. I don't know what General Perisic meant. You're showing me a document that I've not seen before, a document issued by the Army of Yugoslavia, not by the VRS. And finally, you want me to explain things that concern equipment, whereas my area of responsibility was the personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Absolutely right, General. However, you did testify on direct examination about the effect of this blockade, about the sanctions that were imposed in August 1994. And that's why I'm exploring this topic with you. Let's look at another document, if we can.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please show the witness Exhibit P851. We don't seem to have a B/C/S version on the screen. Maybe it's coming now. There we are. Can that be enlarged a bit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You'll see, General Skrbic, this is a document addressed by General Perisic to commander of the Republika Srpska Main Staff, and it says -- it's dated the 22nd of February, 1995. But in the first paragraph you'll see that General Perisic is referring to a decision from mid-September 1994 that the supreme council took to suspend the payment of salaries to "your people." But then General Perisic says: "We have agreed that I send you 500.000 dinars, which I did on 21 September. And the money was collected by General Tomic." So we see here at least an effort by General Perisic to try to continue with salary payments for members of the VRS; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. This is not much. This is very little money, and I believe that you had Mr. -- General Borijovanic [as interpreted] as a witness. He was in a position to explain how could the Chief of General Staff, be it General Perisic or General XY, how he could dispose with 500.000 dinars. That was part of some reserves. I can't explain, but any finance guy can explain how a Chief of the General Staff has petty cash, as it were, and allocate those funds wherever they wanted. However, when it cam to the big money, the budget of the military, he could not distribute or allocate money from that. I did see this document, Mr. Saxon; Mr. Lukic showed it to me. And I told him that I had not been aware of this document and also that I had not been aware of that money allocation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. First of all, no one by the name of General Borijovanic has testified to date in this trial, but I want to explore something that you said. You mentioned part of -- that this payment was part of some reservist, and so if I understand your testimony, the Chief of the General Staff has a certain amount of money allocated to him called reserves or what have you. And the Chief of the General Staff then, at least at this time during the war, had the discretion to use those reserves how he saw fit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And Mr. Lukic is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, let me correct the -- and say that the witness mentioned General Boro Jovanovic. That's my first correction. The second thing that I want to say and object, it seems that the witness himself has said that he was not a relevant authority on the area. So whatever you now ask him may only call of speculation as to what the Chief of General Staff could do with his reserves. Let me just add one more thing. The witness was talking in principle about what any Chief of General Staff anywhere in the world can do, so he was laying down a principle, a standard. Calling for any other detail is simply calling for speculation on the part of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Two responses, Your Honour. I think I should be able to ask the witness whether he is able to answer my question. And second of all, I object to what was clearly Mr. Lukic now putting words available for the witness. I don't think that was appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Objection sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: May we please show the witness Exhibit P1257.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Skrbic, you'll see this is a document dated the 27th of February, 1995. It's signed by lieutenant -- it's signed by a person representing Lieutenant Commander Ojdanic -- Lieutenant-General Ojdanic. It's addressed to a military post in Kragujevac. And it says on the basis of a ruling, and there's a particular number dated the 24th of February, 1995, "by the Chief of the General Staff of the VJ," it says "... please issue to the 30th Personnel Centre from military post 5292 Mrsac the following ..." And the items to be issued are 100 rounds of 152-millimetre contact fuses. And down below it gives a dead-line for the realisation of the task as 28 February 1995. You told Mr. Lukic during your direct examination -- or actually you affirmed today that your position is only humanitarian assistance was crossing the border between the FRY and Republika Srpska after the blockade was imposed. This document suggests that in addition to humanitarian assistance, military materiel was also being sent to the RS, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not able to answer that question, but it doesn't say that it's going to Republika Srpska, but rather to the Kragujevac TRZ, which stands for maintenance and repair centre or department in Kragujevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Skrbic, it does say at the top beneath the date "to be delivered to the military post at Kragujevac," but then in the next provision it says: "On the basis of the ruling ..." issued on the "24th of February, 1995, by the Chief of the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army, please issue to the 30th Personnel Centre from military post 5292 ... the following ..." And then we see a hundred pieces of 152-millimetre contact fuses. Now, the 30th Personnel Centre stood for the Army of Republika Srpska, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It didn't?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the witness responded in this way because probably due to misinterpretation into B/C/S. So could Mr. Saxon please repeat his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: First of all, may we start with the first principles. When an officer was assigned to the 30th Personnel Centre, that meant that officer was going to serve in the Army of Republika Srpska; isn't that right, General?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So - and I'm grateful to Mr. Lukic - with respect to this document if we have munitions being issued to the 30th Personnel Centre, that means these munitions are going to be sent to the Army of Republika Srpska; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If ammunition or anything of the sort is being sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not disputing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And this document would indicate that ammunition was being sent to the Army of Republika Srpska during the time of the blockade; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I have to comment on this comment even though this is beyond my scope of responsibility. But this is such a confused and imprecise document that all of us here who are making tremendous effort to understand it are find it difficult to understand it. What you read in the first sentence is completely accurate, but then later on when we speak about the rounds please look at the sentence which says "the transportation" to -- "of the ammunition to the TRZ Kragujevac where the take-over will occur is to be done by the issuer using their own motor vehicles." Therefore, in spite of all my efforts towards understanding this document, I still can't fathom certain things that are contained therein. I'm not evading an answer, Mr. Saxon. I'm really doing my best to help you, but I would like to be accurate in trying to help you because this is what I came here for to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, that paragraph which is causing you confusion, doesn't it simply indicate that the personnel at the military post in Kragujevac will obtain the ammunition and bring it to the maintenance and repair department in Kragujevac? Isn't that what the first part of that sentence says?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, according to our interpretation, yes, that could be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then we see the phrase "where the take-over will occur," and that indicates that someone, whether it's a person from the Army of Republika Srpska or someone else, is going to take-over these contact fuses at the maintenance and repair department at Kragujevac; right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I can only guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we move into -- no, it's all right to remain in public session. Can we please show the witness P2746, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Skrbic, this document -- excuse me, this Prosecution exhibit has several pages to it. This first page, you'll see, it's dated the 7th of October, 1995. It's from the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. It's from Commander Ratko Mladic and it's addressed to the command of the General Staff of the VJ, Chief of the General Staff personally. And you'll see, if you look, I believe, in the second paragraph in your version, that General Mladic is saying: "Please send us 10 FAB-275/4 ..." because the VRS does not have any such ammunition. And these are -- it's stated higher up in the text -- there's a reference in the English version to aerial bombs. And can we go to the next page, please, in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've just been informed by my colleague from the Registry that there is no second page. Um -- one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Can we please show the witness then P951.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Skrbic, here we see a document dated the exact same day as the request from General Mladic. It's issued by the office of the Chief of the General Staff of the VJ. It's addressed to the Republika Srpska army Main Staff. It's referencing the document that I showed you a moment ago, the same number and same date. And it says: "The collection of ten pieces of FAB-275/4 is hereby approved. You can collect them yourself from the 608th Logistics Base." And it's signed by the chief of the cabinet of the -- chief of the General Staff, Colonel Borovic. Now, these two documents would indicate that military materiel was moving from the FRY to the Army of Republika Srpska during the period that the blockade was in place; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not right, Mr. Saxon. This is dated 9th October 1995. That was the most difficult period for the Army of Republika Srpska, and I believe that that was the period when preparations for the Dayton Accords were underway. And then again, would you please not ask me about the documents that contained information beyond my responsibility. This is the first time that I'm seeing this document. This is the first time that I'm hearing about the request for this ten pieces of equipment. The things were calming down because the Dayton Accords were in the offing. Many things in this respect are not clear to me and what is not clear to me I'm reluctant to try and to explain to you. That was, as you can see, towards the end of 1995. We are talking about October.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, General Skrbic. One last --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would that be -- okay, one last.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It is one last question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The sanctions, the blockade between the FRY and the Army of Republika Srpska, was still formally in place in October of 1995; right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we take the first break, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll take the break and come back at quarter to 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Skrbic, I'd like to move to a different topic now. I'd like you to turn your mind back to your testimony from last week. On last -- last Wednesday - this is at pages 11691 through 11692 - you and Mr. Lukic discussed a group of officers from the VJ who arrived in the Republika Srpska in mid-July 1995 who were to be assigned to posts in the Army of Republika Srpska. And on page 11693 at lines 14 to 18 you described how Bogdan Sladojevic was first sent to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps and then after several days he was transferred to the Main Staff of the VRS, and from the Main Staff of the VRS you explained that Bogdan Sladojevic was then sent to the Drina Corps. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Mr. Saxon. Only I didn't mean that he was sent to the Drina Corps. He was sent to join the units of the Drina Corps because he received certain tasks. He was assigned to the Main Staff of Republika Srpska after having been at the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I want to make sure that the record is clear and that there's not a problem in interpretation. It's perfectly clear where you say "he," Mr. Sladojevic, "was sent to join the units of the Drina Corps because he received certain tasks." But then, according to the English interpretation, it then says: "He was assigned to the Main Staff of Republika Srpska after having been at the Drina Corps." And I understood your testimony from last week that first Mr. Sladojevic was assigned to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, and then after several days in the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps Mr. Sladojevic was transferred to the VRS Main Staff; and then from the VRS Main Staff, Mr. Sladojevic was transferred to the Drina Corps, pursuant to an order, as a representative of the VRS Main Staff. Have I correctly summarised this chain of events?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely and exactly you have summarised it, but he was never assigned to the Drina Corps. As for the rest, it is all correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. In fact, General Mladic ordered that Colonel Sladojevic and two other colonels, Colonel Trkulja and Stankovic, go to the Drina Corps in July 1995 to assist the Drina Corps, in particular the 1st Zvornik Brigade, in the planning and co-ordination of combat operations with Muslim forces in the wider areas of Kamenica and Cerska; isn't that right? That was the reason for which Colonel Sladojevic had to go to the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, Mr. Saxon. Only I learned about that from an expert analysis compiled by Mr. Richard Butler.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Right. And it was important at that time, which is -- and this is why General Mladic sent these three experienced officers to the 1st Zvornik Brigade, what was needed at the time was a plan to comb the terrain and block and destroy, if you will, the remaining parts of armed Muslim groups in that area. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only guess about that, and I'm not willing to give you a reply on that basis because I was not privy to those issues at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. I want to talk to you, General Skrbic, about the issue of VRS personnel returning to the Army of Yugoslavia. Last week at page 11776 of the transcript starting at line 10, Mr. Lukic asked you: "Was General Perisic or anybody else from the VJ able to order you or anybody else from the VRS to go back to the VJ without prior consent of Ratko Mladic?" And this was your response: "First of all, he couldn't issue such an order because there was no such relationship between General Perisic and the Army of Republika Srpska. He could ask the commander of the Main Staff of the VRS whether a certain officer could be transferred if he really needed that officer. To be fully clear, General Perisic could not order me, General Skrbic, to go back to the Army of Yugoslavia." Do you recall that testimony, sir?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please show General Skrbic what is Exhibit P2598, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Skrbic, you'll see this is an order --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, if we could zoom in on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's order number 5-193 - and I'd like you to please try to remember that number, please, because we're going to see it again - of the chief of the personnel administration of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia. It's dated the 17th of June, 1994. And you'll see here that this document contains a series of appointments, appointment orders, issued by the personnel administration. And can we please turn to page 9 in the English, please, and page 8 in the B/C/S version. And if we could focus on the bottom of the page in the English version, please, and the bottom half of the B/C/S version as well. Thank you. And you'll see here, General Skrbic -- actually, before we do this, can we go to the last page in both -- in both versions, please. You'll see, General Skrbic, that this order was signed by Major-General Dusan Zoric, and at the time he was the chief of the personnel administration at the VJ General Staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, can we please go to page 9 in the English, page 8 in B/C/S. And focus -- if we could zoom in on the bottom half of each version. You'll see, General Skrbic, that number 13 here refers to a Captain Tihomir Babic, who's being sent or appointed to the Loznica garrison, the 1st Army -- there's a subheading above 13 to the 1st Army, to operations group Drina. And then it says that now Captain Babic has a duty post at the 30th Personnel Centre of the Yugoslav Army General Staff, he's filling an establishment post of a major, as of 10th of November, 1993. Are you able to follow with me, sir?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please go to the next page just in the English version. And if we could zoom in a little bit at the top of the page, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, General Skrbic, if you could focus on the text at the bottom of the page in your version.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Those following in English, please look at the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It says: "Responsible commanding officer will appoint the named person immediately." And then it says: "Upon receipt of the document on appointment, he shall be immediately released from duty as per peace time and sent to the new duty." And then it says below that the last line there: "Rationale: Redeployed as required." Have you been able to follow with me, General Skrbic?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please show General Skrbic Exhibit P1856.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Skrbic, we see that this is a document from the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska from the sector for organisation, mobilisation, and personnel. It's dated the 14th of August, 19 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I am not receiving interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are we able to help? The witness is not receiving interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You'll see, General Skrbic, this is a document from the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, from the sector for organisation, mobilisation, and personnel, and it's dated the 14th of August, 1994. Correct me if I'm wrong, this is the day before you took over your duties as the chief of this sector; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And we see below there the document references the same gentleman that we saw a moment ago in the VJ personnel administration order, Tihomir Babic, captain first class. It says: "Execution of an order regarding transfer." And sent to the command of the Drina Corps. And then in the text below it says: "Further to an order number 5-193, dated the 17th of June, 1994 ..." That was the same order that we saw a minute ago. Are you following me, General Skrbic?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it says that Captain Babic is transferred from the 30th Personnel Centre to the -- to the VJ. And then it says: "The aforementioned shall be forthwith discharged from his present unit and dispatched into transfer." And then it's from your predecessor, Major-General Grubor. Now, General Skrbic, first of all, this document shows that Major-General Grubor was executing an order of the chief of the personnel administration of the VJ General Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't show that. He executed an order and I can't remember the name. I suppose that he first received an approval to be transferred to the Army of Yugoslavia from the commander of the Main Staff of the VRS, and then the Personnel Administration Chief of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia issued an order to send him to that unit. And Mico Grubic [as interpreted], my predecessor, regulated his situation in the VRS to be sent there, to be re-assigned to the army, and the rest is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I understand your supposition, but nowhere in this document is there a reference to any kind of approval from the commander of the Main Staff of the VRS, is there?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please show the witness P1855.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And before we look at the next document, General Skrbic, if such an approval, this kind of approval of the commander of the Main Staff was issued, that approval should exist in the personnel file of this person, shouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, such a document is not archived in the personnel file. In my sector, for example, such a document is used to regulate the status in the Army of Republika Srpska, and if he is transferred to the Army of Yugoslavia his authorities in the Army of Yugoslavia use it to regulate his status there, and that is if he's transferred to the Army of Yugoslavia. And second of all, and I apologise for adding things to your question, and that document was not sent to the corps command. The corps command was just verbally informed. In the command of the Drina Corps, if there is possibly such an approval - and as I said, I'm not sure whether we sent them or not, Mico Grubor would be better placed to say what the fact was - it wouldn't be in the Drina Corps. It would be in the Main Staff of the VRS in the sector for organisation, mobilisation, and personnel affairs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have an objection from my client that he is not receiving interpretation, and I must say that I also have problems hearing the witness through the headphones. I can hear him better across the room. There is a problem with channel 6. Could I please hear the interpreters just to check the interpretation. Now it's better. We both are receiving a much better interpretation now. We have a much better reception of the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. And thank you, Mr. Usher. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I want to make sure I understand your testimony. I think I understood you to be saying that the corps command was just verbally informed. Are you saying that your sector with the long name that I'm sure I will butcher if I try to say it, are you saying that for something as important as the redeployment from the VRS back to the VJ, your sector would not receive any written documentation about this in terms of the approval that was given?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Saxon. Just the contrary was the case. We did have documents to that effect. If that person had received an approval from the commander of the Main Staff of the VRS, that approval should be found in the sector where I worked, and the name is a mouthful, so let -- forgive me if I don't say it in full. Sometimes I myself find it difficult to say its full name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see Mr. Lukic is having a problem, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I see Mr. Registrar is trying to communicate with some technicians. I hope we'll get assistance. Mr. Lukic, if you're still not receiving any interpretation, please say, and then we'll issue a stop until technicians have attended to the problem, either you or your client.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At first we could not hear Mr. Skrbic's answer, and now I can hear you and I believe that the situation is the same with Mr. Perisic. I'll keep watch on the developments and I will keep you posted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you get the problem again, just rise. Thank you. Mr. Saxon, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You say, General, that -- let me go back to my earlier question. Actually, we'll work with this document that we have on the screen. This, I believe, is P1855.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's what you called.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You'll see, General Skrbic, this is a document from the Drina Corps command dated the 16th of August, 1994. Again it refers to Captain Tihomir Babic. Again it says "execution of an order regarding transfer." It says "to the command of the 2nd," and then we see an acronym. I'm wondering if you can help us with this, sir. The acronym Plpbr, does that stand for the 2nd Podrinje Light Brigade?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And that was --

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Light infantry brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But my question would be: Is it Podrinje or Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In the English, General Skrbic, the English version of this document after the acronym we see the phrase Prizren Light Infantry Brigade with a question mark, and my question for you is: Should that English version actually say "Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade"?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And again in this order it begins: "Further to order PU," the personnel administration, "confidential number 5-193, dated 17 June 1994," and it says that Captain Tihomir Babic is transferred from the 30th Personnel Centre to the 1st Army, where he will resume a corresponding position. And it's signed by Major-General Milenko Zivanovic, the commander of the Drina Corps. Again, General Skrbic, this document refers to an execution of an order regarding transfer. It refers to the VJ order that we saw a few moments ago. There's no reference at all to any communication from the chief of the VRS Main Staff giving approval for this transfer. Doesn't that indicate -- again we see Major-General Zivanovic executing an order of the VJ?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a mistakenly drafted transfer note. The Drina Corps cannot refer to an order of the personnel administration. It had to refer to an order signed by my predecessor, Mico Grubor. The personnel officer who was in the Drina Corps, his name was Radenko Jovicic. He was my subordinate and he often made mistakes, and I often warned him about that. And here again he made a mistake. He was supposed to refer to an order issued by the Main Staff of the VRS and not the order that he referred to herein. He sometimes bypassed everybody. He communicated directly with the Army of Yugoslavia. Later on we put a ban on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, your predecessor, Major-General Grubor, he was a competent officer, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, no doubt about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: He was a careful man, followed the rules; right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please go back to what is P1856.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Saxon, there were things that he did superficially, and I'm not saying that I was immune to that either. Sometimes I did things half-heartedly and superficially. You know, war does that to people. Mistakes cannot be excluded.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And as you said earlier in your testimony, during your direct testimony, very few requests to be -- for VRS officers to return to the VJ were approved because, as you put it, the VRS did not want to erode the strength of its army. And so the matter of a transfer back to the VJ would have been looked at very carefully; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. So now if we look at P1856 again, this is the document issued by your predecessor, Major-General Mico Grubor, again, as he put it, an execution of an order regarding transfer. And again, what we see Major-General Grubor doing here, as did Major-General Zivanovic, is he's basing his order on the order number 5-193 that was issued by the General Staff of the VJ; right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. You established the correct link here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And the reason that link was important was because when such orders were issued the members of your sector in the VRS Main Staff had to respond to them; correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the moment I joined the sector we executed things only on the approval of the commander of the Main Staff of the VRS. Nobody else's, you can be sure of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please show General Skrbic what is Exhibit P1934. And can we please go to page 11 in the Serbo-Croat version and in the English from -- there are several different excerpted translations in this exhibit, and can we please go to the English excerpt that starts with 0422-8609, page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And maybe what we -- if we could go to page 3 of the B/C/S version, please. One more page in the B/C/S version, please. One more page in the B/C/S version. I just want to show -- this is a personnel file and I want to show General Skrbic the first page. Can we go one more page forward. I need to go forward. I don't need that enlarged. Can we go forward another page, please. There we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You'll see, General Skrbic, that we're going to spend a few minutes looking at the personnel file, the VJ personnel file, of Vujadin Popovic. Do you see his name there, the first page of his file?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, can we please go to page 11 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't see the photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I know, it's too dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we can --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, what we see here, General Skrbic, is part of a table showing the different appointments and positions held by Mr. Popovic during his military career. And you'll see in the third assignment from the top in your version and in the English version as well we see then-Major Popovic being assigned to the 30th Personnel Centre. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we scroll down just a bit in the English version, please. Bit more. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see that that transfer is done pursuant to an order of the personnel administration, the chief of the personnel administration of the Main Staff of the VJ, dated 9 February 1994. Are you able to see that, General Skrbic?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In the column below that we see another entry, where on the far left we see that now it's Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic is being appointed as the assistant head of command and operations in security and intelligence, still in the 30th Personnel Centre. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that, but there is something else here, counter-intelligence and security affairs it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please go to the next page in the English version. And perhaps we could make the first half of the page a bit bigger for those following along in English. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The next entry, still in the 30th Personnel Centre, now it's Colonel Popovic being appointed head of the security department in the intelligence security organ. Is that what that shows, General Skrbic?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Saxon. It says chief of department for security in the organ for security and intelligence services. I've given you the full title. In the corps there were no sectors -- administrations but departments. I wanted you to understand the abbreviation in the way that I've just expanded it, in the way that I've just explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much for clarifying that. And then the next entry, in English it says that Colonel Popovic was dismissed from duty and sent for training in the 46th, I believe it's -- well, I won't -- you know what I'll do, General, I'm going to ask you to read the next entry, please, so that the interpreters can interpret for us so that we make sure that that next entry is accurate. Can you read the next entry in your language, please, can you read it out loud?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can do that, Mr. Saxon. It reads as follows: "Dismissed from duty and sent for schooling in the 46th class of the General Staff school with the centre of military schools in Belgrade a PG," which is salary group 9, PG stands for salary group.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And this is happening in September 1997; right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Then we see the next entry, it's made in July 1998 and apparently Colonel Popovic has finished his schooling because he's now being assigned back to the 30th Personnel Centre in an undetermined station. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is an undetermined duty station.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. But in the next entry, which is pursuant to an order of the 30th of September, 1998, we see that Colonel Popovic is going to become the head of the security -- well, I apologise if the English translation is wrong, but in English it says head of security sector. And then it says in the next column security administration in the 30th Personnel Centre. Is that correct or does that need a correction as well?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to read it as it should be read. I'm sorry. Probably English language cannot faithfully reflect everything. This is what it says: Head of the section for security affairs, security administration of the 30th Personnel Centre of the VJ General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Now I'd like you to please focus on the next entry, which says: "Sent temporarily to the 2nd Army, duty station not determined." And that's pursuant to an order of the VJ personnel administration in the VJ General Staff of the 22nd of April, 1999. Now, if we just focus on this particular transfer, first of all, this reference to the 2nd Army, that's the 2nd Army of the VJ; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, Colonel Popovic did not have to re-enlist in the VJ when he was sent to the 2nd Army; correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. As you said, the 2nd Army was part of the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Up until this point, Colonel Popovic had been a member of the 30th Personnel Centre, and that means that he was serving in the Army of Republika Srpska; right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a member of the VRS and his status was regulated by the 30th Personnel Centre. Up until 1999 he maintained that status, as you put it correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And up until -- when he returned -- when he was sent temporarily to the 2nd Army of the VJ in April of 1999, he did not have to re-enlist in the VJ, did he?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he had to. How else would he be receiving his salary?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, if this gentleman had to re-enlist, then there would have to be, for example, documentation of that re-enlistment, right, in his personnel file?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there are lots of documents kept in personnel files, but not all of them. That's why you have all these boxes and you have all these references to relevant orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, when he -- when he was sent temporarily to the 2nd Army of the VJ in April 1999, would a new officer's commission have been issued for general -- for Colonel Popovic?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. Not necessarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So in summary, an officer like in this case Colonel Popovic, who's being transferred back from the VRS to the VJ wasn't required to go through the normal processes of induction into an army at that time?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean by "normal processes."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, give me a minute then. For example, in accordance with Article 14 of the Law of the VJ -- actually, one moment, that's not the right article. Article 21 of the Law of the Army of Yugoslavia, subtitled: "Entry into Professional Military Service." And it says: "A citizen of Yugoslavia who fulfils the following general requirements may enter into service as a professional soldier ..." And then there are a series of criteria that are listed, if he has appropriate qualifications, for example, if he's medically fit to serve in the army, if there are no criminal proceedings instigated against him, if he has performed his compulsory military service or regulated his military service in another way. There was no need for Colonel Popovic to establish this -- these criteria in April of 1999, was there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon -- okay. Mr. Lukic first.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can see that the interpreters are having problems with these terms. I think that we should put this on the screen in front of the witness so that he can see the exact wording of this article of the law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand that to the extent that we are able to respond to that we can do that. But, Mr. Saxon, I don't have the piece of law before me, but hearing what you say I thought you were saying enter into military service. This to me sounds like initial entry, a new person who's just qualified and is getting into the army for the first time, not a transfer of a person who's already within the army. You see, I have another problem because people -- this 30th Personnel Centre is supposed to be regulating soldiers who are physically working in the VRS, and these transfers that are taking place that you have been referring to, they talk of 30th Personnel Centre, they talk of VJ, and the 30th Personnel Centre is said to be in Belgrade. You know, and we have seen before that people are said to be in the 30th Personnel Centre Belgrade in the VJ, when in fact they are in the VRS. Now, I'm not quite sure how we go about understanding a document like this one which is so cryptic in just column forms and not in a narrative way just what is happening. You know, because we're having this person who we know qualified in the VJ, is working in the VRS, his personnel file is controlled by the 30th Personnel Centre. If indeed he's going from the VRS to the VJ, does the VJ have to go through that process of an initiate, when in fact this is their soldier whom they had loaned to somebody else?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, that was essentially the question that I wanted to put next to the witness, but perhaps he could respond to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, I know I've confused the whole thing, but that's the confusion that's going on in my mind as I try to follow the trend of the story. But are you able to come to our rescue, Mr. Skrbic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm glad that you yourself completely comprehend the situation. As an illustration let me tell you this: If somebody joined the VJ, he didn't have to join again any other army. At the time we had the VJ, now we have the Army of Serbia, then there was the Croatian army, then there was the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. People from the JNA joined all these army without having to enlist again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, we understand that, Mr. Skrbic. For the time being we're not talking about the Army of the BiH or the Army of Croatia. Let's try and stay with the VRS and the VJ, because to me it seems like there is movement backwards and forwards between the VRS and the VJ here. And my question really is: If a soldier - and I want to suspect that Mr. Popovic will have gone into the army at -- for the first time when it was still called the JNA, then it became the VJ, then as part of the VJ was transferred to the 30th Personnel Centre to work in the VRS. Now, if this table here is documenting his transfer back to the VJ, my biggest problem is two questions. First of all, what Mr. Saxon asked you, does he have to go through the process that Mr. Saxon explained, they check his criminal record, they check whether he's got qualifications? Now, this is the man who qualified with them to the JNA. Do they check his qualifications again, do they check all these things. That's the first point, that's the question by Mr. Saxon. My question again is: How do we determine in fact that this person is going back to the VJ when in fact certain posts in the VRS are described as VJ posts Belgrade, 30th Personnel Centre, when in fact we know that the person is in the VRS? How do we determine without a narration that this is a real transfer or maybe just an intent of it. That's the question I find -- I would like to be -- to have answered. But first I turn to Mr. Saxon's question. Does a JNA soldier who qualified as a JNA who is in the VRS have to go through the process that Mr. Saxon referred to when he's transferred back to the VJ, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Are you able to explain or how are we to determine what actually is happening from this table without a narration, where some of these posts are used -- the names are used interchangeably? In other words, a person is said to be working for the VJ 30th Personnel Centre in Belgrade, when in fact we know he's in the VRS. And then when you talk of a transfer to the -- to head security administration -- okay, this one says 30th Personnel Centre. If he goes back, is he going back to the VJ or is he still in the VRS? Because saying head of security sector, security administration 30th personnel General Staff of the VJ Belgrade 707, you could either be in the VRS or you could be in the VJ. We don't know. And unless there is a narrative that explains this, then we understand that -- yeah, okay. Let me refrain from saying that. But how do we know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, you cannot conclude that from these documents. I can tell you that de facto he was the head of the security administration of the General Staff of the VRS, but that's something that I know. However, this is the format used to regulate his status in order for him to receive all the benefits, social security, salary, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah. I think the witness's answer just confirms my confusion and my difficulty. I'm not sure whether you want to take the matter any further, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I may take it just a bit further, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you could.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you could, I would be very happy.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see in this table here, General Skrbic, that Colonel Popovic was the head of the security administration in the 30th Personnel Centre beginning in September 1998, although you've just explained that you knew -- you are aware that de facto he was serving in the VRS beginning in that time. That's clear. But then in the next entry from April 1999 we see that Colonel Popovic is sent temporarily to the 2nd Army of the VJ. And the point that I think that I would like to try to make is that there was no need for Colonel Popovic to go through any enlistment process, qualification process, when he moved temporarily from the Republika Srpska to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia because formally Colonel Popovic had never left the Army of Yugoslavia. Is my point correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, according to his formal status, he didn't leave the VJ; but de facto, he was a member of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: De facto during these years where it says here that he was assigned to the 30th Personnel Centre, Colonel Popovic was physically serving in the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Now I want to ask you the following.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please show the witness what is P191.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Skrbic, this is the Law on the Army of Republika Srpska, which I'm sure you're familiar with. Help us with this, there's nothing in the Law on the Army of Republika Srpska, at least as it existed during the war, that provides that members of the VRS can be sent to serve in foreign armies, is there?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
